reasoning: gcd(2^m-1, 2^n-1) = 2^gcd(m,n)-1. gcd(35,91)=7, so the answer is 2^7-1=127. Verified directly: gcd(2^35-1, 2^91-1)=127.
The product is 29!. The power of 10 is limited by the power of 5: floor(29/5)+floor(29/25)=5+1=6, while the power of 2 is far larger. Verified by stripping trailing zeros from 29!: exactly 6.

The equation is x^2 - bx + (c-5) = 0, so sum = b and product = c-5. (alpha-beta)^2 = b^2 - 4(c-5) = 25, giving b^2 = 4c - 20 + 25 = 4c + 5. Verified symbolically: the squared root difference is b^2 - 4c + 20.
No milk-drinker takes tea, so |T and M| = 0 and hence |T and C and M| = 0. Inclusion-exclusion: 75+60+50-15-|C and M| = 150, so |C and M| = 20. Milk only = 50 - 20 = 30.

The first train crosses a MAN (a point), so only the first train's 200 m length matters; the 150 m is a distractor. 200/(v1+v2)=10 and 200/(v1-v2)=20 give v1+v2=20 and v1-v2=10, so v1=15 m/s = 54 km/hr.
Set the common value to k: a=k/2, b=k/3, c=k/6, d=k/9, e=k/12, f=k/18. (a+b) = 5k/6 and (c+d+e+f) = k(6+4+3+2)/36 = 5k/12, so the ratio is 2.

Take 100 bananas at cost 1 each (CP 100). 88 remain and are sold for 104 (4% profit), so the selling price is 104/88 = 13/11 each. Selling all 100 at that price gives 1300/11 = 118.18, i.e. a profit of 200/11 % = 18 2/11 %.
(5+3sqrt2)(5-3sqrt2) = 25-18 = 7, so alpha = sqrt7. Then 8 + 2sqrt7 = 7 + 2sqrt7 + 1 = (sqrt7 + 1)^2, whose positive square root is sqrt7 + 1 (numerically 3.6458 both ways).

If 5 divides none of n-1, n, n+1 then n = 2 or 3 (mod 5), so n^2 = 4 (mod 5) and n^2+1 = 0 (mod 5). Checked against all such n below 60: only n^2+1 is always divisible by 5; the other three options fail.

Totals 30*65 = 1950 and 35*70 = 2450 give 4400; correcting the 74 to 47 removes 27, giving 4373 over 65 students = 67.2769, i.e. approximately 67.28.

Triangle inequality gives a+b > c, so (sqrt a + sqrt b)^2 = a+b+2sqrt(ab) > a+b > c, hence sqrt a + sqrt b > sqrt c and the expression is STRICTLY positive - it can never be 0. 200,000 random valid triangles produced no non-positive value. RUNNER-UP C ('Non-negative'): this option is also a true statement, since positive implies non-negative, so the paper offers two true options and relies on the convention that the tightest description wins. C would win only if the setter intended the weaker claim; B is the precise answer and the one the strict inequality supports.
LCM(15,25,35,45) = 1575 minutes. In 72 hours = 4320 minutes, floor(4320/1575) = 2 further coincidences (at 1575 and 3150 minutes).

a^n - b^n is divisible by a-b = 83. Also 97^30-14^30 = (97^2)^15 - (14^2)^15 is divisible by 97^2-14^2 = 83*111 = 83*3*37, so 37 divides it too. Both confirmed by direct computation.

n^3-n = (n-1)n(n+1), three consecutive integers, divisible by 6. n^5-n is divisible by 5 by Fermat's little theorem. n^5-5n^3+4n = (n-2)(n-1)n(n+1)(n+2), five consecutive integers, divisible by 5! = 120. All three verified over n = -50..49.

Half-yearly compounding: 4 periods at 10%, amount 10000*(1.1)^4 = 14641, so CI = 4641. Simple interest at 20% p.a. for 2 years = 4000. Difference 641.

reasoning: Expanded symbolically: the x^2 coefficient is a(b-c)+b(c-a)+c(a-b) = 0, so statement 1 holds. The x coefficient is (a-b)(a-c)(b-c), which equals MINUS (a-b)(b-c)(c-a); at a=1,b=2,c=3 it is -2 while (a-b)(b-c)(c-a) = +2. Statement 2 is therefore wrong by a sign, so only 1 is correct. NOTE: this is a plausible paper defect - a setter using the identity a(b^2-c^2)+b(c^2-a^2)+c(a^2-b^2) = (a-b)(b-c)(c-a) and forgetting the leading minus would key C.

1 - x - x^n + x^(n+1) = (1-x) - x^n(1-x) = (1-x)(1-x^n). Since (1-x) divides (1-x^n), the product is divisible by (1-x)^2 = 1-2x+x^2, and it is obviously divisible by 1-x^n. Polynomial division for n = 1..7 gives remainder 0 in both cases.
mx^2 + (m+8)x + 9 is a perfect square when its discriminant vanishes: (m+8)^2 = 36m, i.e. m^2 - 20m + 64 = 0, giving m = 4 and m = 16.
Symbolic simplification of (x-a)^2 - (y-b)^2 with the given x and y returns exactly b^2. Spot-checked at (a,b) = (2,1), (3,1), (3,2), each giving b^2.

1 is FALSE: cos^4 - sin^4 = cos 2theta, but 2tan/(1-tan^2) = tan 2theta. 2 is TRUE since cosec^2 - cot^2 = 1. 3 is TRUE since (1-tan^2)/(1+tan^2) = cos 2theta = cos^2 - sin^2. With tower height h, the car is at h*sqrt3 when the depression is 30 degrees and at h when it is 45 degrees, so it covers h(sqrt3 - 1) in 6 minutes. The remaining distance h then takes 6/(sqrt3-1) = 3(sqrt3+1) = 8.196 minutes, which lies in 8 < t < 8.3.

CAVEAT - the TRUE supremum is slightly above 24pi: an SLSQP optimisation over all nine parameters from 3000 random starts reaches 24.0770pi with radii 4, 2.14359 and 1.86603 (the second circle tangent to the big one in the corner at r = 16 - 8sqrt3 = 2.14359), and I reproduced that configuration independently by hand at 24.06. Statement II: (x+y)^3 < 16 admits 0, -4, -8, ... , again 'No'. Under standard data-sufficiency logic each statement alone answers the question asked. reasoning: q^2+q = q(q+1) is always even, so p^2+q^2+q is odd exactly when p is odd. reasoning: Statement I restates the midpoint theorem, which holds in EVERY triangle, so it carries no information and cannot decide the question. Statement II gives angles 30, 60, 90, so the triangle is right angled - a definite Yes. Exactly one statement alone suffices.

Statement II: the perpendicular 6.72 on the longest side 25 gives area 84; Heron with sides 25, 24, x and area 84 yields x = 7 or x = 48.51, and the latter is excluded because 25 and 24 are stated to be the two LONGER sides - so x = 7 uniquely. Statement I is therefore inconsistent with the stem as printed. RUNNER-UP A: if Statement I is judged defective/inconsistent, only Statement II works and the answer is A.

N = 20, so N/2 = 10 falls in class 60-90 (cf before = 9, f = 7): median P = 60 + (10-9)/7*30 = 450/7 = 64.2857. Mode Q = 72, so Q - P = 54/7 and 7(Q-P) = 54 = 9R, giving R = 6.

Read the figure on page 13 (0-based): the right angle is at B, D lies on AC with BD perpendicular to it, and the circle centred at B meets BC at Q. 6-8-10 is right angled at B, so BD = 6*8/10 = 4.8 = BQ, and QC = BC - BQ = 8 - 4.8 = 3.2 cm.

y = 15 gives x = 3y = 45, so the central angle AOB = 180 - x - y = 120 degrees. C lies on the major arc, so the inscribed angle ACB is half of it: 60 degrees. Verified numerically with C placed at 230, 250, 270 and 290 degrees - every position returns exactly 60.0 degrees.
